- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 378	## Warmup Wave (F13-F22): gem5-style `--vsim-warmup-icount`
379	
380	Motivation: today vsim's reported cycle figure (`mcycle` delta across the ROI)
381	includes the cold-cache/cold-BPU/cold-TLB prefix at vsim entry. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`
382	and `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` document this as an accepted limitation.
383	gem5's equivalent is `--warmup-insts N`: run N functional insns on the
384	fast-forward CPU, then `m5.stats.reset()` at the switch boundary. Hybrid_sim's
385	constraint differs: QEMU has no cache model, so warmup MUST happen inside vsim.
386	The solution is a measurement-start snapshot of `mcycle/minstret` K insns after
387	vsim entry; cache stays warm because vsim is one process, only the stats
388	window moves. Wire format size is preserved (uses bytes from `reserved[232]`).

# ROADMAP: gem5 CPU-Switch Parity

Tracks 22 independent features to extend hybrid_sim (QEMU + vsim) with the four
CPU-switch mechanisms from `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md`. F1-F12
are the gem5-parity core (CSR/PC/icount/SimPoint switching); F13-F22 add
gem5-style `--vsim-warmup-icount` so the reported cycle figure excludes the
vsim cold-cache prefix. One session = one feature. Update status when
starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).

## Status Legend

- not-started: feature has not begun
- in-progress: currently being implemented in a session
- done: behavioural+structural commits landed and tests pass

## Dependency DAG

```
F1 ----+----> F4
F2 ----+
F3 ----+
F5 ----+----> F6
       +----> F7 ----> F12 ----> F11
       +----> F8 ----> F9 ----> F10

F13 (ABI) --+--> F14 (snapshot) --+--> F15 (vsim CLI) --+--> F17 (e2e CSR)
            |                     |                     +--> F18 (e2e PC)
            +-----> F16 (drain) --+                     +--> F19 (e2e icount, also needs F5,F6)
                                  |
                                  +--> F20 (orchestrator)  +--> F22 (docs; needs F17..F21)
                                                           +
F15 ----------------------------> F21 (hsim driver) -------+
```

Migration order: ship F1, F2, F3 first (infrastructure layer). After that,
F5/F6/F7 parallelise across sessions because they touch independent files.
F12 (SimPoint binary integration) sits between BBV emission (F7) and
slice-consume (F11) because F11's slice indices come from SimPoint's
clustering output.

Warmup wave (F13-F22) runs after F1-F12. F13 is the load-bearing structural
gate; F14-F16 are the three independent leaf landings on top of it; F17-F21
parallelise across sessions; F22 closes the wave once green.

## Features

### F1 - Rebrand plugin drain-exit code 0 -> 200

- Status: done
- Type: structural
- Description: Today `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261` exits 0 on drain;
  workload completion and drain are indistinguishable. vsim already exits
  200 (`verilator/src/hybrid/exit_codes.hpp:7`). Bring the plugin in
  line. The orchestrator (F2+) relies on this distinction.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261`
  - `tests/e2e.sh` (exit-code assertions)
  - `tests/e2e.sh`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a test in `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh` runs
  the plugin with a CSR fixture and asserts QEMU exits with code 200.
  Fails on today's 0.

### F2 - Orchestrator skeleton (Python package)

- Status: done
- Type: structural (new code)
- Description: Create `tools/orchestrator/` Python package. CLI parsing,
  plan loading from YAML, dry-run that prints the planned spawns. No real
  spawn yet.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/__init__.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/plan.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_plan_parses.py` loads
  `examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` and asserts the resulting `Session` has
  three `Step` entries. Fails because no parser exists.

### F3 - ctypes ABI binding + state-file validator

- Status: done
- Type: structural (new code)
- Description: Mirror `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`'s `hybrid_state_v1` in
  Python via ctypes. Field-offset asserts at import time. Add
  `validate_state_file(path)` checking magic 0x42594841, version 1,
  exact `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)` bytes. Wire into orchestrator as the
  post-spawn gate.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/abi.py` (new)
  - `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (read-only)
  - `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h` (read-only; mirror its asserts)
- Dependencies: F2
- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_abi_roundtrip.py` writes a known
  `hybrid_state_v1` struct from a small C harness, reads it in Python,
  asserts all fields (GPRs, FPRs, CSRs, V-state) match. Fails until
  ctypes layout matches C.

### F4 - Orchestrator runs today's CSR fixture end-to-end

- Status: done. The in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490` (later
  renumbered to `:530-542`) was removed in the F4-cleanup pass: see
  `f4_cleanup.md`. `tests/e2e.sh` now invokes
  `python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume` for the QEMU2 leg;
  `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`, its doctest, and the obsolete
  `rt_no_qemu_binary` / `rt_gdbstub_timeout` / `rt_pty_handback` drivers
  are deleted. Python gdbstub remains the canonical state-restore path.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: Replace one `e2e.sh` invocation with
  `orchestrator run <yaml>` for `rt_c_v_regs`. Add the C++ helper
  `tools/hybrid_apply_state` extracted from `qemu_handback.hpp`'s
  state-restore body. Delete the in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490`;
  vsim returns 200 cleanly.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py`
  - `tools/hybrid_apply_state/` (new C++ CLI; lifts from
    `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp:287-335 apply_state`,
    `:41-63 pick_free_port`)
  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:478-490` (delete)
  - `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:108-238` (add CTest variant)
- Dependencies: F1, F2, F3
- TDD RED: `ctest -R rt_c_v_regs--orchestrator` is registered but the
  orchestrator's spawn path is incomplete; test fails. Then asserts
  exit-code parity with `rt_c_v_regs--csr` (the bash-harness version).

### F5 - icount counter + trigger in QEMU plugin

- Status: done. Trigger priority (spec section 5 row 1: CSR/PC > BBV >
  icount) is deferred - F5 registers icount tick FIRST in
  `vcpu_tb_trans`, so it wins on insns where both fire. The F5 e2e uses
  a CSR-less fixture, so this is invisible today; F11 (slice-consume)
  will revisit when BBV ties enter the picture.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: Add `uint64_t icount_retired` incremented in a per-insn
  callback registered alongside the CSR/PC matcher in
  `vcpu_tb_trans()`. New plugin arg `icount=N`. When
  `icount_retired >= icount_target`, set the should-exit flag and call
  `on_handoff` at the same insn boundary.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264-300` (`vcpu_tb_trans`)
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:302-339` (arg parser)
- Dependencies: F1
- TDD RED: `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_icount_trigger.sh` runs a fixture
  with `--plugin-args icount=100000` on a CSR-less binary; asserts the
  drained state file's `minstret >= 100000` and exit code is 200. Fails
  because the `icount=` arg is unknown.

### F6 - vsim IcountTrigger (sibling of CsrTrigger)

- Status: done. `HandoffController` was retrofitted to a class template
  on the trigger type (structural; CTAD preserves all existing call
  sites). `IcountTrigger` lives at `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp`
  with the duck-type surface (`lookup`, `empty`, `observe_commit`).
  `--hybrid-icount N` is wired in `main.cpp` and dispatches into
  `Simulator::enable_hybrid_icount_handoff`. Mutually exclusive with
  `--hybrid-exit-pc`. Unit test
  `tests/hybrid/icount_trigger.test.cpp` covers both the standalone
  trigger and the templated controller's drain.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: New `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` with the
  same duck-type surface as `CsrTrigger` (`lookup(pc) ->
  std::optional<hit>`, plus an `observe_commit()` that increments the
  per-hart counter). `HandoffController` is already template-parameterised
  on trigger type (`handoff_controller.hpp:38`). Add

## Warmup Wave (F13-F22): gem5-style `--vsim-warmup-icount`

Motivation: today vsim's reported cycle figure (`mcycle` delta across the ROI)
includes the cold-cache/cold-BPU/cold-TLB prefix at vsim entry. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`
and `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` document this as an accepted limitation.
gem5's equivalent is `--warmup-insts N`: run N functional insns on the
fast-forward CPU, then `m5.stats.reset()` at the switch boundary. Hybrid_sim's
constraint differs: QEMU has no cache model, so warmup MUST happen inside vsim.
The solution is a measurement-start snapshot of `mcycle/minstret` K insns after
vsim entry; cache stays warm because vsim is one process, only the stats
window moves. Wire format size is preserved (uses bytes from `reserved[232]`).

## Bug Audit Wave (2026-05-26) (B1-B20)

Findings from a three-agent code audit (QEMU plugin + ABI, vsim C++
orchestration, hsim driver + shell). Scope: bugs in *working* modes only
(CSR / PC / icount / SimPoint). Known limitations from `CLAUDE.md` are
excluded: vsim phase trap-free + PMP-static, little-endian only,
HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64, no syscalls in phase-2 ROI, JOBS=8 cap.

Severity ladder:

- CRITICAL: round-trip breaks or silent state corruption on the golden path
- HIGH: wrong cycle count or wrong end state on a plausible workload
- MEDIUM: edge cases (large/empty/zero inputs, unusual env)
- LOW: latent / unreachable today, kept for future-proofing

Each bug below was either spot-verified by re-reading the cited code, or
flagged `Verification needed:` when the agent's line numbers could not be
confirmed in this audit pass. Fix sessions should re-verify before
implementing.

### B1 - Check `exec_progbuf()` return value at four PB call sites

- Status: done (2026-05-26)
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Type: behavioural
- Description: `exec_progbuf()` returns `bool` (declared at
  `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:100`). Four call sites
  discard the return: `resume_driver.hpp:109` (vsetvl for V CSR
  restore), `resume_driver.hpp:167` (PB fallback inside
  `write_csr_abstract_or_pb`), `program_buffer.hpp:164` (vsetvl prep
  in `pb_v_data_sweep`), and `program_buffer.hpp:171` (per-register
  vle8.v / vse8.v loop). A failed PB execution leaves vtype / vl /
  vstart and the V data regs in inconsistent state with no signal to
  the caller, silently corrupting any subsequent V op.
- Key files:
  - `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:109,167`
  - `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:164,171`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a doctest using `recording_bus` that forces a non-zero
  cmderr on the next abstractcs read after the PB submit, then calls
  `pb_v_data_sweep` and asserts the function reports failure rather
  than silently returning. Today the test cannot fail because the
  call site never inspects the return.
- Fix: rewrote `exec_progbuf` to throw `std::runtime_error` on
  post-exec cmderr instead of returning `bool` (return type now
  `void`). All four call sites propagate via stack unwinding; no
  per-site patches needed. RED:
  `program_buffer.test.cpp` "exec_progbuf: throws when cmderr set
  after execution" + resume-level regression
  `resume_driver.test.cpp` "resume throws when V-data sweep Program
  Buffer execution fails" (arms `fail_next_pb_exec` on the
  RecordingBus). GREEN: 16/16 host-runnable hybrid unit tests pass.

- Status: done (2026-05-26)
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Type: behavioural
- Description: `tests/e2e.sh:96-103` launches QEMU1 with `-nographic`

  group (`( ./tests/e2e.sh ... ) &`) and asserts it completes within

  owns the tty.
- Fix: added `</dev/null` before the existing output redirect on
  both the QEMU1 (`-nographic`) and the vsim (`timeout`-wrapped)

file.content:
# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document

Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.

Companion docs:
- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - engineering plan
- `docs/limitation.md` - current ROI envelope (alpha)

This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
capex requirement

**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
RTL learning curve."

---

## 2. Product Definition

What the customer buys:

| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint |
| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |

What the customer does NOT get:
- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
- Andes RTL or microarch internals
- Source of the cycle engine
- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)

---

## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas

### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |

### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |

### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer

| Role | What they care about |
|---|---|
| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, SimPoint coverage, kanata output |
| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |
| **Engineering VP / buyer** | total cost vs FPGA capex, support SLA, lifecycle |
| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |

---

## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity

Rough TAM estimate (top-down):

- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M

Adjacent expansion:
- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.

---

## 5. Competitive Positioning

### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)

| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled SimPoint/kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |

Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.

Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
a paid product.

### 5.2 The wedge

Three things competitors do not deliver together:

1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas
   require customer integration work; Wind River is functional-only.
2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium
   need a $M+ board.
3. **Bundled SimPoint + kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors
   sell these as separate add-ons or do not ship them at all.

### 5.3 Honest losses

- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
  Mitigation: SimPoint clustering shrinks effective ROI.
- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0
  is a fresh product. Mitigation: design-partner program before
  general availability.

---

## 6. Business Model

### 6.1 Pricing structure

Three SKUs:

| SKU | Audience | Includes | Price guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HybridSim Workstation** | per-seat developer | full feature set, 1 named seat | $40K-80K/yr |
| **HybridSim Project** | per-project team | floating license pool (5-25 seats) | $200K-1M/yr |
| **HybridSim Academic** | universities, labs | feature-limited (no kanata export, no SimPoint estimate report) | $5K-15K/yr |

Add-ons (post-v1.0):
- Linux/SMP support pack (multi-hart, S/U-mode beyond v1.0 envelope)
- Custom Andes IP variant support (one-off NRE)
- Premium SLA (24h response, dedicated FAE)

### 6.2 License enforcement

- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm
- Node-locked option for air-gapped customers (HSM-bound)
- Floating pool with checkout / checkin
- Per-feature flags (kanata, SimPoint, vendor CSR pack)
- License expiry triggers graceful shutdown with checkpoint export

### 6.3 Delivery channels

- Direct (Andes sales) for top-50 accounts
- Distributor / reseller for long tail (e.g. through Andes regional
  partners in Japan, EU, US)
- Evaluation: 30-day full-feature trial under EULA, node-locked

---

## 7. Market Requirements

Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
relative to v1.0 ship.

### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads

Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.

- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.

### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI

Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
measure, hand back to QEMU.

- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.

### MR-C - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint

Long workload, no explicit ROI. SimPoint clustering picks
representative regions, cycle engine measures each, weighted
combine produces a whole-program estimate.

- Acceptance: weighted estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL on at
  least 3 SPEC-class workloads.

### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)

Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.

### MR-E - Andes vendor CSR and ACE parity

All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.

### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)

Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.

- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
  the post-warmup window.

### MR-G - Iterative microarch tweak loop

Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
checkpoint without re-running boot.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
  reference workload.

### MR-H - Multi-hart support

At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.

### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility

Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.

- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.

### MR-J - CI / batch integration

The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.

- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.

### MR-K - First-class observability

Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
error".

- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
  log message identifying the corrupted register and the handoff
  phase. No silent failures.

---

## 8. Go-to-Market & Delivery

### 8.1 Design-partner phase (months 0-6 post-engineering complete)

- 3-5 named Andes customers under NDA evaluate pre-GA build
- Free use under design-partner agreement; required to give
  feedback and bug reports
- Goal: prove MR-A + MR-B on real customer workloads before GA

### 8.2 Controlled GA (months 6-12)

- Direct sales to ~10 accounts at full price
- Quarterly feature releases
- Dedicated FAE per top-3 account

### 8.3 Broad GA (year 2+)

- Distributor channel opens
- Academic SKU launches
- Add-on packs (multi-hart, vendor IP variants) release

### 8.4 Onboarding goal

Customer goes from license activation to first valid cycle figure
on their own workload in **under 1 working day** with documentation
alone, no FAE intervention.

---

## 9. Success Metrics

### 9.1 Product KPIs

| Metric | v1.0 target | Year-2 target |
|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock speedup vs vsim-alone (1% ROI workload) | 100x | 1000x |
| Per-ROI accuracy vs fully-RTL | <= 1% | <= 0.5% |
| SimPoint whole-program accuracy | 5-10% | 3-5% |
| Time-to-first-result for new user | 1 day | 2 hours |
| Determinism rate across hosts | 100% bit-identical | 100% bit-identical |

### 9.2 Business KPIs

| Metric | Year-1 | Year-3 |
|---|---|---|
| Paying accounts | 3 | 11 |
| ARR | $300K | $2M-5M |
| Design-partner -> paying conversion | 60% | 75% |
| Customer renewal rate | n/a | >= 80% |
| Net Promoter Score | n/a | >= 30 |

---

## 10. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encryption tooling adds 6-12 months | ship slip | high | start encryption track in parallel with engineering Wave 1; consider Carbon-style external partner |
| ZeBu price compression for RISC-V mid-market | margin erosion | medium | deepen Andes IP integration; sell on TCO not list price |
| Imperas under Synopsys expands into Andes IP | direct competitor | medium | move first; lock design partners |
| Customer demands ISA beyond Andes | scope creep | medium | charter Andes-only for v1.0; revisit at v2.0 |

# Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification

Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.

Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.

Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
one or more MR-x in MRD.md.

---

## 1. Scope and Definitions

### 1.1 In scope

Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:

- `hsim` driver CLI
- QEMU (Andes fork) with hybrid plugin
- vsim cycle engine (Verilator-derived, encrypted)
- State transport library (`hybrid_state_v1`)
- Trigger toolkit (magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint)
- Pipeline trace converter (kanata, Clarity DB)
- License daemon
- Installer, documentation, sample workloads

### 1.2 Out of scope (v1.0)

- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants
- QEMU + Alioth (cycle-side Alioth) - documented as future in MRD
- FPGA backend
- Cloud-hosted SaaS delivery
- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster
- Vector extension `V` beyond what AndeStar V5 covers

### 1.3 Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| ROI | Region of Interest. Window of dynamic instructions to measure cycle-exactly. |
| Fast engine | QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin. Runs non-ROI code. |
| Cycle engine | vsim, encrypted Verilator-derived binary. Runs ROI. |
| Handoff | Atomic state transfer between fast and cycle engine. |
| Trigger | A mechanism that fires the handoff (magic-CSR write, PC match, icount expiry, SimPoint marker). |
| Hybrid state | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format - GPR, FPR, V-state, CSR, PC, mem snapshot, timing baseline. |
| Cycle figure | The cycle count delta across the ROI window, returned to the user. |
| Warmup | Initial cycles after handoff where cache/predictor state is not yet steady; excluded from acceptance comparison. |

### 1.4 Traceability

Every FR includes a `Traces: MR-x [, MR-y...]` line tying it back
to `MRD.md`.

---

## 2. System Architecture Overview

```
+--------+   trigger   +----------+   handoff   +--------+
|  ELF   | ----------> |   QEMU   | ----------> |  vsim  |
| (cust) |             |  + plug  |  state +    | cycle  |
+--------+             +----------+   mem mmap  | engine |
                            ^                   +--------+
                            |   handback             |
                            +------------------------+
                                state + cycle count
```

Three phases per workload:
1. **QEMU1**: boot + setup, fast.
2. **vsim**: ROI, cycle-exact, encrypted.
3. **QEMU2**: post-ROI, fast (optional, for whole-program runs).

Shared substrate: `/dev/shm` mmap-backed RAM, file-descriptor
based state transport (`hybrid_state_v1`), license daemon over
network socket.

---

## 3. FR-1xx Functional Capabilities

### FR-101 - Three-phase handoff orchestration

`hsim run` shall execute the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 sequence
without user intervention beyond the initial invocation.

- Inputs: ELF, ROI specification (trigger config), workload args
- Output: cycle figure (decimal), exit code, optional pipeline trace
- Acceptance: a bare-metal kernel with PC-trigger round-trips end-to-end with exit code 0.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-102 - Trigger: magic-CSR write

A write to a configured CSR (default `0x7C0`, customer-configurable)
shall fire the QEMU->vsim handoff at the next instruction boundary.

- Acceptance: ELF that writes magic-CSR triggers handoff within 1 instruction; no false positives in 1B-cycle stress test.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-103 - Trigger: PC watchpoint

A configured PC address shall fire the handoff at the matching
instruction without requiring source modification.

- Acceptance: closed-source ELF (no magic-CSR access) triggers correctly on PC match.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-D (closed-source customer ELFs)

### FR-104 - Trigger: instruction count

A configured icount threshold shall fire the handoff after N
dynamic instructions from a reference point.

- Acceptance: handoff fires at exactly icount=N, deterministic across runs.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-I

### FR-105 - Trigger: SimPoint cluster marker

The SimPoint clustering tool shall generate a per-cluster trigger
spec consumable by `hsim run --mode simpoint`.

- Acceptance: SimPoint output drives N handoffs at N cluster boundaries; per-cluster cycle figures collected and weight-combined.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-106 - QEMU1 -> vsim handoff: full state transport

The following state shall transport bit-exactly from QEMU to vsim:

- 32 GPRs (RV64I)
- 32 FPRs (with NaN-boxing per RISC-V spec)
- V-state (vector regs + vcsr per AndeStar V5)
- All architectural CSRs reachable in supported privilege modes
- All Andes-vendor CSRs in the customer-visible list (see FR-401)
- PC
- Memory snapshot (shared mmap RAM)
- PMP config (read-only, enforced at vsim entry)
- Trap delegation state

- Acceptance: post-handoff vsim execution of `nop` produces identical architectural-visible state as a fully-RTL run from the same checkpoint.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E, MR-I

### FR-107 - vsim -> QEMU2 handback

Symmetric to FR-106. State at vsim ROI exit shall be re-injected
into QEMU2 bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: bare-metal workload completes execution under QEMU2 after a vsim ROI window; final result matches fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-108 - M-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall include any RV64GC + AndeStar V5 workload
running entirely in M-mode with PMP-static, trap-free ROI.

- Acceptance: 10 representative M-mode kernels round-trip without error.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-109 - S-mode and U-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall extend to S-mode and U-mode workloads,
including supervisor page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and trap handling
inside the ROI.

- Acceptance: 3 Linux userspace workloads (SPEC-class) round-trip.
- Traces: MR-B

### FR-110 - Cycle figure reporting

After every successful run, `hsim` shall emit:
- Total ROI cycles (decimal)
- Per-phase wall-clock time
- SimPoint weighted estimate (when applicable)
- Confidence band on the estimate (95% CI)

- Acceptance: machine-parseable JSON report at `hsim.report.json`.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-J

### FR-111 - Pipeline trace export: kanata

When `--trace kanata` is set, the cycle engine shall emit kanata
format for the ROI window, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline
after warmup.

- Acceptance: `diff` against fully-RTL kanata is empty for the post-warmup window.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-112 - Pipeline trace export: Clarity DB

When `--trace clarity` is set, the cycle engine shall emit a
Clarity-format pipeline DB for the ROI window.

- Acceptance: Clarity DB import into the Andes Clarity viewer succeeds; per-stage event counts match fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-113 - Multi-hart ROI

`hsim` shall support ROIs that span >= 4 harts with coherent state
transport through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart kernel round-trips; cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-H

### FR-114 - Resumable / checkpointed runs

A long QEMU1 phase shall be checkpointable mid-run, so a customer
can boot once and re-enter vsim multiple times without re-booting.

- Acceptance: customer boots Linux once (~30 min), then runs 10
  different ROIs measured against the same checkpoint, with total
  wall-clock under 1 hour.
- Traces: MR-G

## 4. FR-2xx Performance Requirements

### FR-201 - Wall-clock speedup envelope

On a workload where the ROI is <= 1% of dynamic instructions,
HybridSim shall complete in <= 1% of the wall-clock time of a
vsim-alone run of the same workload.

- Acceptance: 3 reference workloads measured; speedup >= 100x.
- Traces: MR-A, MRD section 9.1

### FR-202 - Per-ROI accuracy

The cycle figure for the ROI window shall agree with a fully-RTL
baseline within 1% after a documented warmup tolerance.

- Acceptance: 5 reference ROIs; max error <= 1.0%.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E

### FR-203 - SimPoint whole-program accuracy

The weighted whole-program estimate from SimPoint mode shall be
within 5-10% of fully-RTL on SPEC-class workloads.

- Acceptance: 3 SPEC-class workloads; max error <= 10%, average <= 5%.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-204 - Time-to-first-result

A new customer with the installer and a sample workload shall
produce a valid cycle figure within 1 working day, with
documentation alone (no FAE involvement).

- Acceptance: timed user study with 3 fresh engineers; 100% reach valid figure within 8 hours.
- Traces: MRD section 8.4

### FR-205 - Iterative re-measurement latency

After an initial QEMU1 phase, a re-measurement of the same ROI
with an updated cycle engine shall complete in <= 5 minutes.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle measured on 3 microarch parameter tweaks.
- Traces: MR-G

## 5. FR-3xx Interface Requirements

### FR-301 - `hsim` CLI

Top-level entry. Subcommands:
- `hsim run` - one-shot workload execution
- `hsim simpoint` - clustering + per-cluster runs + combine
- `hsim trace` - trace-only mode (kanata, clarity)
- `hsim checkpoint` - QEMU1 checkpoint management
- `hsim license` - license daemon control / diagnostics
- `hsim diag` - capture bug report bundle
- `hsim version` - prints versions of all components

- Acceptance: `--help` for every subcommand; exit codes per Unix convention.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-302 - Configuration file format

`hsim.config.yaml` shall specify trigger config, workload paths,
cycle-engine params, license server, output format. Schema-validated.

- Acceptance: bad config produces actionable error pointing at the offending line.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-303 - JSON output report

Every run shall emit `hsim.report.json` with the schema defined in
`docs/report-schema.json` (to be written).

- Acceptance: schema validation passes on every successful run.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-304 - Programmatic API (Python binding)

A Python module shall expose the `hsim run` interface as a function
returning the report dict. For CI scripting.

- Acceptance: `import hsim; r = hsim.run(...)` returns a parsed report.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-305 - Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | run succeeded, valid cycle figure |
| 1 | configuration error |
| 2 | license error |
| 3 | trigger never fired |
| 4 | state-transport corruption detected |
| 5 | cycle engine crashed |
| 6 | QEMU engine crashed |
| 7 | ROI exited unexpectedly |
| 9x | reserved |

- Acceptance: each documented failure produces the matching exit code in a fault-injection test.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

## 6. FR-4xx Compatibility Requirements

### FR-401 - Andes IP coverage

v1.0 shall support these Andes cores: AX25, AX27, AX45, AX46.
D23v deferred to v1.1.

For each core, the Andes vendor CSR set published in the AndeStar
V5 specification (revision frozen at v1.0 ship) shall round-trip
bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite (~50 CSRs per core) passes 100%.
- Traces: MR-E

### FR-402 - ACE coherence support

Multi-hart workloads shall transport ACE coherence state
(directory + snoop filter) bit-exactly across the handoff.

- Acceptance: a coherent multi-hart test (e.g. shared-counter benchmark) produces identical results to fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-E, MR-H

### FR-403 - Host OS support

v1.0 ships for x86_64 Linux only. Supported distros: Ubuntu 22.04
LTS, RHEL 8 and 9, SUSE SLES 15. No Windows, no macOS.

- Acceptance: install + smoke test passes on each supported distro.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-404 - Toolchain compatibility

ELFs produced by:
- Andes GNU toolchain (current and previous release)
- Andes LLVM toolchain (current release)
- Upstream RISC-V GCC (current release)

shall be accepted.

- Acceptance: a benchmark built with each toolchain round-trips.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-405 - QEMU upstream tracking

The QEMU engine shall be based on QEMU 9.x, with documented
patch set against upstream. Customer can rebuild from source under
NDA (source escrow).

- Acceptance: source tarball + patch series builds against upstream 9.x.
- Traces: MRD section 12 (QEMU dependency)

## 7. FR-5xx IP Protection Requirements

### FR-501 - Cycle-engine binary encryption

The vsim binary shall not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch
internals by static or dynamic analysis.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit; legal sign-off.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-502 - Anti-debug / anti-instrumentation

The cycle engine shall refuse to execute under `ptrace`, `gdb`,
`strace`, dynamic tracing, or memory-introspection tools beyond
those explicitly whitelisted for support telemetry.

- Acceptance: attempted attach produces an actionable refusal log; no crash, no leak.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-503 - State-transport encryption

`hybrid_state_v1` payload in `/dev/shm` shall be encrypted at rest
with a session key derived from license activation. Plaintext
visible only within the cycle engine address space.

- Acceptance: external readers of `/dev/shm` see ciphertext; the cycle engine reads it correctly.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-504 - License key binding

The cycle engine binary shall refuse to execute without a valid
license check-out from the license daemon. License key is bound to
host MAC + HSM (node-locked) or floating pool (network).

- Acceptance: missing or invalid license produces exit code 2 with a clear message.
- Traces: MR-J, MRD section 6.2

### FR-505 - License feature flags

License records shall carry per-feature flags:
- core support pack (which Andes cores)
- kanata export
- SimPoint
- multi-hart
- premium SLA (telemetry-routed)

Cycle engine shall enforce flags at runtime.

- Acceptance: a license without kanata flag refuses `--trace kanata` with exit 2.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-506 - License expiry

License expiry shall:
1. Refuse new runs (exit code 2).
2. Allow in-progress runs to complete with a warning log.
3. Not corrupt or drop reports already written to disk.

- Acceptance: clock-skew test (advance host clock past expiry mid-run) shows graceful behavior per spec.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-507 - Source escrow

For top-tier customers, source for the cycle engine shall be
deposited with a neutral escrow agent and released on documented
trigger events (e.g. Andes EOL of the product).

- Acceptance: escrow agreement signed; release procedure documented.
- Traces: MRD section 12

## 8. FR-6xx Quality & Observability

### FR-601 - Structured logging

Every internal event (trigger fire, handoff begin/end, state
transport, license check, error) shall log in the format
`[Tag] evt=<ns>.<action> key=value ...`.

- Acceptance: a regex-based log validator passes on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-602 - Log levels

Log levels: ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE. Default INFO. Settable
via `--log-level` or `HSIM_LOG_LEVEL` env.

- Acceptance: level filtering observable on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-603 - Bug report bundle

`hsim diag` shall capture:
- All log files
- The active config
- The `hybrid_state_v1` snapshot (encrypted, support-only readable)
- Host info (uname, distro, libc, kernel, license daemon state)
- Reproducer ELF and config (with customer opt-in)

into a single tarball ready to attach to a support ticket.

- Acceptance: support reproduces a customer-reported bug from a `hsim diag` bundle alone.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-604 - Deterministic mode

When `--deterministic` is set, every run with the same inputs
produces bit-identical cycle figure, pipeline trace, and report
across hosts and runs.

- Acceptance: cross-host reproducibility test (3 hosts) passes.
- Traces: MR-I

### FR-605 - Error message quality bar

Every fatal error shall include:
- a unique error code (e.g. `HSIM-E0042`)
- a one-line description
- a pointer to the doc section that explains it
- the suspected failing component
- recommended next step (retry, contact support, check config)

- Acceptance: a sample of 20 deliberate errors are graded against the bar; >= 90% pass.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-606 - Telemetry (opt-in)

With explicit customer opt-in, `hsim` may transmit anonymized
usage data (workload size, success/failure code, host info) to
Andes telemetry endpoint. Default off.

- Acceptance: telemetry disabled by default; opt-in via config flag; payload schema documented and signed-off by legal.
- Traces: MRD section 8

A single self-extracting installer (`.run` or `.deb` / `.rpm`)

## 14. Open Engineering Questions

For Engineering / IP officer review:

- **Encryption mechanism**: in-house obfuscation pass on Verilator
  output, or external Carbon-style partner? Trade-off:
  build-vs-buy, royalty vs salary, time-to-market.
- **License daemon**: build on FlexLM (industry standard but
  licensing fee), Reprise RLM, or in-house? FlexLM has highest
  customer acceptance.
- **State-transport encryption key**: derive from license daemon
  on each run, or fixed per install? Per-run is more secure but
  adds latency.
- **vsim binary size**: encrypted output is typically 2-5x source
  size; what is the acceptable footprint?
- **Multi-hart determinism**: scheduling order in vsim cycle engine
  is deterministic given seed; QEMU side may not be. Strategy?
- **Vendor CSR list**: FR-401 says "published in AndeStar V5"; need
  a frozen list per core for the v1.0 commit.
- **Source escrow**: which neutral agent (Iron Mountain, NCC, etc)
  and what are the customer-facing trigger conditions?

279	- SimPoint output includes CI bands.
280	- Submodule drift fails CI.
281	- cmderr default behavior is fail-loud.
282	
283	---

286	
287	Only pulled in if a customer asks. Otherwise documented as
288	"v1.0 supports andes_ae350 + ax45mpv + x86-64 host".
289	
290	- L10 - parameterize V scratch GPA, machine name, CPU model.
291	- L18 - byte-swap path + ABI hash check at handoff.
292	- L13 - RVC marker (no action until RVC adds a CSR write encoding).
293	
294	---

297	
298	- CI matrix: add a second host config by end of Wave 5.
299	- Release notes per wave.
300	- Customer-visible changelog: which fixtures now work that did not.
301	- Migration guide for v1 -> v2 wire format (Wave 1).
302	- Update `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` at the end of every wave.
303	- Move closed limitations out of `limitation.md` into a separate
304	  `docs/limitations_closed.md` for traceability.
305	
306	---
307

309	
310	| Wave | Weeks | Cumulative | Headline                              |
311	|------|-------|------------|---------------------------------------|
312	| 0    | 2     | 2          | Stop silent wrongness                 |
313	| 1    | 4     | 6          | v2 wire format                        |
314	| 2    | 12    | 18         | OS-bearing workloads (S-mode + traps) |
315	| 3    | 4     | 22         | Andes parity                          |
316	| 4    | 4     | 26         | Multi-hart + bigger workloads         |
317	| 5    | 4     | 30         | Accuracy + determinism                |
318	| 6    | -     | -          | Portability (deferred)                |
319	
320	### Two ship targets
321	
322	- **Minimum viable beta (6/10 commercial)**: Wave 0 + Wave 1 +
323	  L3 + L4 + L6 from Wave 2. About 4-5 months.
324	  Covers: FP correctness, S-mode workloads, traps inside ROI.
325	  Does NOT cover: full Linux, multi-hart, Andes vendor CSRs.
326	
327	- **Commercial v1.0 (8/10)**: Waves 0-5. About 7-8 months.
328	  Matches the earlier "6-9 month hardening track" estimate.
329	
330	---
331	
332	## Dependencies (Mermaid-style ASCII)
333	
334	```
335	Wave 0 (silent-wrongness fixes)
336	   |
337	   v
338	Wave 1 (v2 wire format)
339	   |
340	   +----> Wave 2 (ROI envelope: L1-L6 use v2 trap/priv/S-mode blocks)
341	   |
342	   +----> Wave 3 (Andes parity: L21 uses v2 ANDES block)
343	   |
344	   v
345	Wave 4 (scale: needs v2 hart-id array)
346	   |
347	   v
348	Wave 5 (accuracy + robustness)
349	   |
350	   v
351	Wave 6 (portability - optional)
352	```
353	
354	Wave 1 is the single hard dependency for everything after Wave 0.
355	Waves 2 and 3 can run in parallel once Wave 1 lands (different
356	feature bits, no code overlap).

  pending at the trigger (clear error, no silent miscompare).
- Phase 2 (post-v1): carry reservation in the wire format.
- Files: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (reservation check),
  `state_abi_v2.h` (reservation field, behind a feature bit).

### L1 - syscalls / semihosting in ROI
- Policy choice (decide before implementation):
  - (a) Passthrough: vsim catches semihosting `ebreak`, forwards to
    a syscall trampoline that proxies to the host. Heavy, slow,
    accurate.
  - (b) Detect + warn + skip: vsim recognises the semihosting magic
    triple and skips it with a logged warning. Cheap, lossy.
- Recommend (a) for v1.0 commercial; (b) for the v0.x interim.
- Files: `verilator/src/hybrid/semihosting.hpp` (new), platform
  trap handler hook.

### Wave 2 exit criteria
- A Linux-userspace fixture (S/U-mode + paging) round-trips.
- A trap-on-purpose fixture survives the handoff.
- A PMP-protected fixture enforces protection inside vsim.
- A `printf` call inside ROI runs without a trap loop (under policy a).
- core-rule paragraph in `limitation.md` rewritten as
  "what the ROI now supports".

---

## Wave 3 - Andes parity  (4 weeks)

Goal: vendor-specific CSRs round-trip; trigger does not collide.

### L21 - Andes CSR subset
Categorise each CSR as `software-visible` (must restore) or
`microarch-only` (drain + handback only, no vsim restore needed):

| CSR          | Category        | Notes |
|--------------|-----------------|-------|
| `mxstatus`   | software-visible| extends mstatus; restore on resume |
| `mdcause`    | software-visible| set on Andes-specific traps |
| `mnvec`      | software-visible| non-vectored trap entry |
| `mslideleg`  | software-visible| Andes delegation extension |
| `mmsc_cfg`   | microarch       | feature discovery; usually RO |
| `mcache_ctl` | microarch       | toggles I$ / D$; affects cycle figure |
| `mmisc_ctl`  | microarch       | branch predictor, prefetcher |
| `micm_cfg`   | microarch       | I-cache config (RO) |
| `mdcm_cfg`   | microarch       | D-cache config (RO) |

- Files: `state_abi_v2.h` ANDES_CSR block; `hybrid_handoff.c` Andes
  handles; `resume_driver.hpp` Andes restore path (software-visible
  only); QEMU fork to ensure feature XML advertises all of them.

### L12 - trigger redesign
- Move trigger off CSR `0x7C0` (which is a real Andes CSR).
- Options:
  - (a) Dedicated debug CSR (e.g. `dscratch1` with magic value).
  - (b) Special marker instruction (e.g. `fence iorw, iorw` with
    immediate magic).
- Keep CSR-0x7C0 mode behind a `--trigger=legacy-7c0` flag for one
  release.

### Wave 3 exit criteria
- An Andes-specific feature (e.g. cache enable toggle, hardware
  prefetcher) round-trips with the cycle figure changing accordingly.
- No trigger collision for code that legitimately writes `0x7C0`.

---

## Wave 4 - Scale  (4 weeks)

### L8 - multi-hart
- Per-hart state arrays in v2 wire format.
- Per-hart icount trigger.
- BBV emit per hart.
- Files: every file that references hart 0 implicitly
  (`resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `bbv_emit.h:9`).

### L7 - mmap auto-size + bounds
- Read ELF segment sizes at startup, set mmap accordingly.
- Fail-loud if `--mmap-size` is smaller than required.

### L9 - MMIO in ROI
- Interconnect watch with an allowlist (UART, PLIC, timer).
- Calls outside allowlist abort with a clear error.

### Wave 4 exit criteria
- 2-hart fixture round-trips.
- A 256 MB fixture works without manual `--mmap-size`.
- MMIO miss aborts cleanly with file/line of the offending access.

---

## Wave 5 - Accuracy and robustness  (4 weeks)

### L14 - SimPoint accuracy
- Default `--vsim-warmup-icount` to a non-zero value (tune per phase
  length).
- Add CPI variance / 95% confidence interval to the JSON output.
- Re-validate phase-CPI bias on at least 3 SPEC-like workloads.

### L17 - gdbstub robustness
- `--gdbstub-timeout` flag (default 30 s, was 10).
- Port pick: bind-then-pass-fd-to-QEMU, not close-then-bind (closes
  the TOCTOU window).

### L19 - determinism / drift / fault-injection
- Byte-identical run check in CI (10 reruns of one input).
- `scripts/check_submodules.sh` gates QEMU / vsim / SimPoint SHAs.
- Fault-injection harness: partial drain, disk-full, mmap truncated
  mid-run.
- SIGALRM watchdog around the gdbstub handshake to kill zombie QEMU2.

### cmderr policy
- Change `clear_cmderr_if_set` to fail by default.
- Add `--cmderr=tolerant` flag for the current swallow behavior.
- Diagnostic side channel (B17) becomes a CI signal, not a hidden
  counter.

### Wave 5 exit criteria
- 10 back-to-back runs produce byte-identical state files.
- SimPoint output includes CI bands.
- Submodule drift fails CI.
- cmderr default behavior is fail-loud.

---

## Wave 6 - Portability  (deferred past v1.0)

Only pulled in if a customer asks. Otherwise documented as
"v1.0 supports andes_ae350 + ax45mpv + x86-64 host".

- L10 - parameterize V scratch GPA, machine name, CPU model.
- L18 - byte-swap path + ABI hash check at handoff.
- L13 - RVC marker (no action until RVC adds a CSR write encoding).

---

## Cross-cutting infrastructure

- CI matrix: add a second host config by end of Wave 5.
- Release notes per wave.
- Customer-visible changelog: which fixtures now work that did not.
- Migration guide for v1 -> v2 wire format (Wave 1).
- Update `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` at the end of every wave.
- Move closed limitations out of `limitation.md` into a separate
  `docs/limitations_closed.md` for traceability.

---

## Effort and ship-date summary

| Wave | Weeks | Cumulative | Headline                              |
|------|-------|------------|---------------------------------------|
| 0    | 2     | 2          | Stop silent wrongness                 |
| 1    | 4     | 6          | v2 wire format                        |
| 2    | 12    | 18         | OS-bearing workloads (S-mode + traps) |
| 3    | 4     | 22         | Andes parity                          |
| 4    | 4     | 26         | Multi-hart + bigger workloads         |
| 5    | 4     | 30         | Accuracy + determinism                |
| 6    | -     | -          | Portability (deferred)                |

### Two ship targets

- **Minimum viable beta (6/10 commercial)**: Wave 0 + Wave 1 +
  L3 + L4 + L6 from Wave 2. About 4-5 months.
  Covers: FP correctness, S-mode workloads, traps inside ROI.
  Does NOT cover: full Linux, multi-hart, Andes vendor CSRs.

- **Commercial v1.0 (8/10)**: Waves 0-5. About 7-8 months.
  Matches the earlier "6-9 month hardening track" estimate.

---

## Dependencies (Mermaid-style ASCII)

```
Wave 0 (silent-wrongness fixes)
   |
   v
Wave 1 (v2 wire format)
   |
   +----> Wave 2 (ROI envelope: L1-L6 use v2 trap/priv/S-mode blocks)
   |
   +----> Wave 3 (Andes parity: L21 uses v2 ANDES block)
   |
   v
Wave 4 (scale: needs v2 hart-id array)
   |
   v
Wave 5 (accuracy + robustness)
   |
   v
Wave 6 (portability - optional)
```

Wave 1 is the single hard dependency for everything after Wave 0.
Waves 2 and 3 can run in parallel once Wave 1 lands (different
feature bits, no code overlap).
