1	# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations
2	
3	What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
4	hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
5	the current code (not just the older audit notes).
6	
7	How this file relates to the others:
8	
9	- `docs/TODO.md` - the engineering fix backlog (failure modes `F-T*`). It is
10	  the *plan to fix*. This file is the *plain-English "do not do this" list*.
11	- `ROADMAP.md` - feature roadmap. Its bug-audit wave `B1-B20` is fully closed,
12	  so those are NOT limitations anymore. The open items live in `docs/TODO.md`.
13	
14	Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
15	line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow
20	
21	This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
22	consequence of it.
23	
24	When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
25	part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
26	FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
27	`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
28	`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.
29	
30	So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
31	be:
32	
33	- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
34	- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
35	- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
36	- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
37	- No system calls / semihosting
38	- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
39	- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)
40	
41	If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
42	wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## State coverage: what the wire format carries
47	
48	Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
49	`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
50	(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
51	the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`), and the QEMU2 handback
52	(`tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`).
53	
54	### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`
55	
56	- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
57	- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
58	  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
59	- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
60	- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
61	- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
62	- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed
63	
64	### NOT in the wire format at all
65	
66	- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
67	  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
68	- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
69	- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
70	  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
71	- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
72	  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.
73	
74	### Carried but NOT restored into vsim
75	
76	The struct holds them so they survive QEMU1 -> QEMU2, but `ResumeDriver`
77	writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:
78	
79	- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
80	  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).
81	
82	Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
83	mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).
84	
85	### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free
86	
87	Four surfaces, four ceilings:
88	
89	| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
90	|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
91	| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
92	| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
93	| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |
94	| QEMU2 handback  | gdbstub P-packet by NAME                      | silently skipped if stub omits the name (L16); `vl / vtype` already needed a QEMU fork patch |
95	
96	Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":
97	
98	1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
99	   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
100	2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
101	   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
102	   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
103	   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
104	   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
105	   the cycle figure.
106	
107	Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
108	CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
109	"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
110	redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload
115	
116	### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)
117	
118	- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
119	  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
120	- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
121	  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
122	  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
123	  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
124	- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
125	  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
126	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
127	  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.
128	
129	### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)
130	
131	- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
132	  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
133	- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
134	  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
135	  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
136	  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
137	  the vsim window only.)
138	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
139	- Status: OPEN.
140	
141	### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI
142	
143	- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
144	  almost anything under an OS.
145	- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
146	  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
147	  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
148	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
149	  `resume()` never writes it.
150	- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
151	  PMP-static but not paging).
152	
153	### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)
154	
155	- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
156	  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
157	- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
158	  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
159	  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
160	  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
161	  the ROI starts from reset values.
162	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
163	  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
164	- Status: OPEN.
165	
166	### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)
167	
168	- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
169	  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
170	- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
171	  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
172	  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
173	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
174	- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
175	  at the trigger.
176	
177	### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)
178	
179	- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
180	  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
181	  it, while running FP code inside.
182	- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
183	  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
184	  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
185	  reset value (RNE, no flags); QEMU2 keeps QEMU1's pre-trigger value
186	  with no sync. FP results inside the ROI use the wrong rounding;
187	  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
188	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
189	  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
190	  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
191	- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
192	  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
193	  enabled, drain before handback.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up
198	
199	### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)
200	
201	- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
202	  trigger boundary.
203	- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
204	  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
205	  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
206	  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
207	  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
208	  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
209	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
210	- Status: OPEN.
211	
212	### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)
213	
214	- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
215	  shared memory.
216	- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
217	  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
218	  corruption.
219	- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
220	  ELF size against it.
221	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.
222	
223	### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)
224	
225	- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
226	  sync.
227	- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
228	  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
229	  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
230	  both.
231	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
232	  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
233	- Status: OPEN.
234	
235	### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)
236	
237	- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
238	  any aliased/device memory.
239	- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
240	  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
241	  device state then disagrees with vsim.
242	- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
243	- Status: OPEN.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits
248	
249	### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU
250	
251	- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
252	  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
253	- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
254	  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
255	  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
256	  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
257	  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
258	  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
259	  these per machine.
260	- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
261	- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.
262	
263	### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)
264	
265	- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
266	  or any future config change to VLEN.
267	- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
268	  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
269	  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
270	  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
271	  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
272	  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
273	- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
274	- Status: OPEN.
275	
276	### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0
277	
278	- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
279	  immediate 0 or 1.
280	- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
281	  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
282	  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
283	  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
284	- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
285	- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.
286	
287	### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)
288	
289	- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
290	- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
291	  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
292	  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
293	  this gate must change together.
294	- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
295	- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.
296	
297	### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement
298	
299	- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
300	  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
301	- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
302	  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
303	  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
304	  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
305	  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
306	     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
307	     CPI is biased high.
308	  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
309	     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
310	- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
311	- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.
312	
313	### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)
314	
315	- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
316	  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
317	  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
318	- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
319	  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
320	  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
321	  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
322	  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
323	  CSR `0x7C0` is also actively repurposed by the trigger matcher (L12)
324	  instead of being preserved.
325	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
326	  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
327	  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
328	- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
329	  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
330	  software-visible (must round-trip).
331	
332	---
333	
334	## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps
335	
336	### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)
337	
338	- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
339	  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
340	- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
341	  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
342	  against the drained state.
343	- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
344	- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").
345	
346	### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name
347	
348	- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
349	  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
350	- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
351	  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
352	  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
353	  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
354	- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
355	- Status: OPEN.
356	
357	### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick
358	
359	- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
360	  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
361	- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
362	  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
363	  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
364	  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
365	  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
366	- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
367	- Status: OPEN.
368	
369	### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only
370	
371	- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
372	  with different struct alignment.
373	- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
374	  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
375	  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
376	  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
377	- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
378	- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).
379	
380	### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)
381	
382	- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
383	  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
384	- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
385	  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
386	- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
387	  mid-run are not covered.
388	- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
389	  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
390	- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.
391	
392	---
393	
394	## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)
395	
396	`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
397	`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
398	and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
399	handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
400	`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
401	the docs will look in the wrong place.
402	
403	---
404	
405	## Quick reference
406	
407	| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
408	|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
409	| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |
410	| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
411	| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
412	| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
413	| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
414	| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
415	| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
416	| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
417	| L9  | MMIO in ROI not handled                 | medium   | open   |
418	| L10 | Hard-wired to andes_ae350 / ax45mpv     | medium   | by design |
419	| L11 | VLEN fixed at 512, mismatch silent      | medium   | open   |
420	| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | inherent |
421	| L13 | CSR marker must be 32-bit               | low      | documented |
422	| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
423	| L15 | No value-level handoff check            | medium   | open   |
424	| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | open   |
425	| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | open   |
426	| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
427	| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
428	| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | open   |
429	| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |
430	
431	---
432	
433	## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)
434	
435	Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
436	Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
437	gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.
438	
439	**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
440	/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**
441	
442	### Axis breakdown
443	
444	| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
445	|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
446	| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Three-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
447	| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
448	| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
449	| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls (L1-L6). |
450	| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
451	| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
452	| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
453	| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `limitation.md` are unusually honest. |
454	| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
455	| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |
456	
457	### What blocks commercial shipping
458	
459	1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
460	   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
461	   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
462	   is observable only through a private counter
463	   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
464	2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
465	   no syscalls inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
466	   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
467	   with page faults.
468	3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
469	   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
470	   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
471	   controls shape the cycle count.
472	4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
473	   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
474	   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`). They exist in the wire format
475	   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
476	   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
477	5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
478	   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
479	   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
480	   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
481	6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
482	   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
483	   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
484	   commercial CI matrix.
485	
486	### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)
487	
488	- Three-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
489	- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
490	- The team writes down what does NOT work (this file, 21 entries plus
491	  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
492	  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
493	- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
494	  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.
495	
496	### Bottom line
497	
498	Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
499	release you need:
500	
501	- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
502	- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
503	- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
504	- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
505	- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
506	- A value-level handoff checker (close L15) wired into CI
507	
508	Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.
509

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
the current code (not just the older audit notes).

How this file relates to the others:

- `docs/TODO.md` - the engineering fix backlog (failure modes `F-T*`). It is
  the *plan to fix*. This file is the *plain-English "do not do this" list*.
- `ROADMAP.md` - feature roadmap. Its bug-audit wave `B1-B20` is fully closed,
  so those are NOT limitations anymore. The open items live in `docs/TODO.md`.

Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.

---

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`), and the QEMU2 handback
(`tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The struct holds them so they survive QEMU1 -> QEMU2, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Four surfaces, four ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |
| QEMU2 handback  | gdbstub P-packet by NAME                      | silently skipped if stub omits the name (L16); `vl / vtype` already needed a QEMU fork patch |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
  the vsim window only.)
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags); QEMU2 keeps QEMU1's pre-trigger value
  with no sync. FP results inside the ROI use the wrong rounding;
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, drain before handback.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
  device state then disagrees with vsim.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
  CSR `0x7C0` is also actively repurposed by the trigger matcher (L12)
  instead of being preserved.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
the docs will look in the wrong place.

---

## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI not handled                 | medium   | open   |
| L10 | Hard-wired to andes_ae350 / ax45mpv     | medium   | by design |
| L11 | VLEN fixed at 512, mismatch silent      | medium   | open   |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | inherent |
| L13 | CSR marker must be 32-bit               | low      | documented |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | No value-level handoff check            | medium   | open   |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | open   |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | open   |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | open   |
| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |

---

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Three-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `limitation.md` are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no syscalls inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Three-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this file, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- A value-level handoff checker (close L15) wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

content.text: [Request interrupted by user]

Read all the planning docs. Here's the landscape and my proposed architecture before I write anything.

## What already exists (don't duplicate)

The engineering half of "all features" is **already broken down three times**:
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6, closing limitations L1-L21
- `docs/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8 (same work, failure-mode view)
- `docs/limitation.md` - L1-L21 plain-English + 4/10 scorecard

And two feature roadmaps are **100% done**: the gem5-parity core (CSR/PC/icount/SimPoint + warmup) and `driver_ROADMAP.md` (hsim CLI F1-F14).

## How the ~50 FRs actually break down today

| Bucket | Count | State |
|---|---|---|
| Core engine + driver | ~13 FRs | **done/partial** (FR-101..108 M-mode, FR-114 checkpoint, FR-301 most hsim subcmds) |
| ROI-envelope engineering | ~9 FRs | **open, already wave-planned** (FR-106 full transport, FR-109 S/U+paging, FR-113 multi-hart, FR-401 Andes CSR, FR-402 ACE = L1-L21) |
| Productization | ~16 FRs | **open, planned nowhere** (FR-302/303/304 config/JSON/PyAPI, FR-112 Clarity, FR-5xx encryption+license, FR-6xx logging/diag, FR-7xx installer) |
| Business / legal / process | ~12 FRs | **open, not code** (FR-507 escrow, FR-8xx support/EOL, FR-9xx audits/signing/export) |

## Proposed core architecture

One **FR-keyed master `ROADMAP.md`** in the house style (F# entries: Status / Type / Description / Key files / Dependencies / TDD RED, grouped into waves, one-feature-per-session). Every feature traces to its FR + MR, so covering all FRs covers all MRs. Status pre-filled from what's already done. The leaf-node detail you review; I fill it.

The two decisions below change the artifact materially, so I need your call.

input.content:
# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing limitations L1-L21
- `docs/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/limitation.md`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

---

## FR -> feature -> status coverage matrix

Every FR in `docs/FRS.md`. `(MR-x)` is the market requirement it serves.

---

## Track and wave ordering (dependency DAG)

```
Track E (engineering)            Track P (productization)        Track B
-----------------------          ------------------------        --------
Wave 0  loud-failure  --+        P-a interfaces (independent)    process /
        (E01..E04)      |        P-b trace export (needs E18)    legal,
           |            |        P-c observability               run in
           v            |        P-d ENCRYPTION  *ship gate*     parallel,
Wave 1  wire v2 (E05) --+----->  P-e licensing (needs P-d)       no code
           |                     P-f packaging (needs all)       dep
     +-----+-----+
     v           v
Wave 2 envelope  Wave 3 Andes
(E06..E11)       parity (E12,E13)
     |           |
     +-----+-----+
           v
Wave 4 scale (E14..E17)
           |
           v
Wave 5 accuracy + robustness (E18..E23)
           |
           v
Wave 6 portability (deferred, see Out of scope)
```

Hard dependencies:

- **F-ENG-05 (wire format v2)** gates Waves 2-4: every new state block
  (trap, S-mode, Andes, per-hart) needs feature-bitted fields.
- **F-PROD-12 (encryption)** is the commercial ship gate (MR-D). Nothing
  goes to a paying customer without it. It is also the longest pole
  (24-48 weeks, possibly an external partner - see MRD open questions).
- **P-e licensing** assumes the encrypted binary exists (P-d) to bind to.
- **P-f packaging** closes last; it bundles every shipped component.

Tracks E, P, and B run in parallel across sessions. Within Track E the
waves are sequential after Wave 1.

---

## Baseline: already shipped

These FRs are closed by the gem5-parity core roadmap (CSR / PC / icount /
SimPoint switching + warmup window) and `docs/archive/driver_ROADMAP.md`
(the `./hsim` driver F1-F14). They are the starting line, not open work.

- FR-101 three-phase handoff (`./hsim run`, M-mode envelope).
- FR-102/103/104/105 all four trigger modes.
- FR-106/107 state transport + handback for the M-mode subset: 32 GPRs,
  32 FPRs, V-state, and 4 restored CSRs (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret).
- FR-108 M-mode workloads (asm + C-runtime fixtures).
- FR-114 checkpoint / replay (`./hsim archive` + `./hsim replay`).
- FR-205 iterative re-measure (replay a checkpoint against a rebuilt vsim).
- FR-301 (partial) subcommands present: list, build, run, test, doctor,
  profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate.

"partial" elsewhere means the M-mode happy path works but the full FR
acceptance (S/U-mode, full CSR set, JSON, RTL-correlated accuracy) is open.

---

# Track E - Engineering

## Wave 0 - Truth in advertising

Goal: stop silent wrongness before fixing big things. Highest ROI per
week. (Absorbs commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 0; L11/L15/L16/L20.)

### F-ENG-01 - Value-level handoff checker

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-K(601), MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L15 (F-T3.1)
- Description: The icount and simpoint paths assert only exit code and PC
  range; a wrong register value passes silently. Add a post-handback
  `g`-packet read in the orchestrator and compare it field-by-field
  against the drained `hybrid_state_v1`. Wire it as a CI gate.
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (post-handback readback),
  `tests/hsim/test_handoff_value_check.sh` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a fixture mutates a GPR mid-ROI; the checker fails when the
  drained struct disagrees with the QEMU2 post-handback readback. Today
  nothing compares them.

### F-ENG-02 - Fail-loud on missing CSR name

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-305 (exit 4), MR-K
- L-id: L16
- Description: GPR/PC writes hard-fail when the stub omits the name, but
  every CSR/PMP/V write goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns
  quietly on a missing feature-XML name. The asymmetry is the hazard.
  Make a missing CSR name raise the same way a missing GPR does, mapped
  to exit code 4 (state-transport corruption).
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:251-258` (`_try_write_u64`
  returns status), `apply_state` (caller asserts)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a mock stub that drops `mtvec`; the orchestrator must raise,
  not skip.

### F-ENG-03 - VLEN runtime check

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L11 (F-T3.4)
- Description: No runtime check that QEMU `vlenb` equals vsim `vlenb`. A
  mismatch leaves the upper bytes of each V register as scratch. Read the
  live `vlenb` at handoff and abort with a clear error on mismatch. Also
  collapse the duplicated `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES=64` constant
  (`checkpoint.py:44`) so it cannot drift from `spawn.py`.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (read live
  vlenb), `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (compare),
  `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:44`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a VLEN=256 fixture against a VLEN=512 sim aborts at the handoff
  boundary instead of silently corrupting the V regfile.

### F-ENG-04 - fcsr / frm / fflags round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-202, MR-A
- L-id: L20 (F-T1.2)
- Description: `fcsr` (packs `frm[7:5]` + `fflags[4:0]`) is in no
  transport surface. FP work inside the ROI uses reset rounding (RNE) and
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong. Add `uint64_t fcsr`, drain
  alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is enabled, drain before
  handback, ship via P-packet.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (field from `reserved[]`),
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (handle + drain),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (drain),
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (handback)
- Dependencies: none (additive in v1; folds into F-ENG-05's base block)
- TDD RED: `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fp_rounding.c` sets `frm=RDN`, does an FP
  op inside the ROI, asserts the result matches RDN not RNE.

## Wave 1 - Wire format v2

Goal: structural foundation. v1 has ~216 reserved bytes and no growth
path; every Wave 2-3 fix needs feature-bitted fields. (Absorbs
commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 1.)

### F-ENG-05 - hybrid_state_v2 with feature bits

- Status: not-started
- Type: structural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-801 (ABI versioning), MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
- L-id: structural foundation (limitation.md "transport ceiling")
- Description: New `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h`. Magic + version + size
  header; reader rejects unknown version. Feature bits extend the three
  existing (`RV64/FP/V`) with `PRIV`, `TRAP_CSR`, `S_MODE_CSR`,
  `ANDES_CSR`. Base block: GPRs, FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs, PC, priv. Trap
  block: mepc, mcause, mtval, dpc. S-mode block (behind bit): stvec, sepc,
  scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip, scounteren, senvcfg, satp. V block
  unchanged. Keep a v1 reader (zero-extend) for one release; drop the v1
  writer after one release. Update all 4 transports (plugin drain, vsim
  resume, vsim drain, orchestrator parse). Mirror in `abi.py`.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (new),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`, `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`,
  `tools/orchestrator/abi.py`, `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`,
  `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`, `docs/wire_format_v2.md` (new)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-04 (fcsr lands in the v2 base block)
- TDD RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts the v2 magic/version header and a
  feature-bit gate (e.g. S-mode block absent when `S_MODE_CSR` clear); a
  v1 blob still reads via the shim. An ABI-hash check fails CI on an
  unreviewed layout change.

## Wave 2 - ROI envelope expansion

Goal: real OS-bearing workloads run inside vsim. Removes the "M-mode only,
trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls" core rule. (Absorbs commercial_v1
Wave 2; L1-L6.)

### F-ENG-06 - Paging (satp) restore + TLB flush

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L3
- Description: `satp` is drained but never written into vsim, so the ROI
  runs bare-mode and every virtual address hits wrong memory. Restore
  `satp` on resume, then `sfence.vma` via the Program Buffer to flush
  stale TLB.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with `satp != 0` runs a Sv39-mapped load inside the
  ROI and reads the correct mapped value.

### F-ENG-07 - Trap / exception state round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L4 (F-T1.4)
- Description: `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are not re-read at drain (stale
  QEMU1 values pass through) and trap-delegation CSRs are not restored, so

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-802, MRD 6.1
- Owner: Support / BU
- Acceptance: Standard / Premium / Mission-Critical tiers each have a
  documented SLA and escalation path.

### F-BIZ-03 - EOL policy

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-803, MRD section 8
- Owner: BU / PM
- Acceptance: each MAJOR supported >= 3 years from GA; EOL announced
  >= 12 months ahead; reflected in license terms.

### F-BIZ-04 - Patch / minor release cadence

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-804, MRD section 8.2
- Owner: Engineering lead
- Acceptance: PATCH every 4 weeks for v1.0, MINOR quarterly; documented
  and trackable in CI.

### F-BIZ-05 - Source escrow

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-507, MRD section 12
- Owner: Legal / BU
- Acceptance: escrow agreement signed with a neutral agent; release
  trigger conditions documented for top-tier customers.

### F-BIZ-06 - Open-source compliance

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-902, MRD section 10
- Owner: Legal
- Acceptance: for every OSS component shipped, license text + source
  pointer + modification disclosure (LGPL Verilator); OSS audit passes.

### F-BIZ-07 - Export control ECCN

- Status: business
- Traces: FR-903, MRD section 6.3
- Owner: Legal
- Acceptance: US EAR / ITAR classification reviewed; ECCN documented;
  installer enforces destination-country checks where required.

### F-BIZ-08 - Design-partner program

- Status: business
- Traces: MRD section 8.1 (no FR; GTM gate for GA)

  build; MR-A + MR-B proven on real customer workloads before GA.

Deferred; documented as limits, pulled in only on customer demand.
